summary: This note surveys the mythical gryphon, a creature with a lion's body and an eagle's head and wings, tracing its origins in the Near East, Egypt and Greece through medieval Christian iconography, literature, art and institutional symbolism. It also covers psychological readings (Jung, Helen Morrison), modern media, and philosophical views of the gryphon as a symbol of balance and protection. The gryphon is presented as a guardian of both physical treasures and the intangible wealth of human potential.
one_line: Overview of the gryphon myth from ancient Near Eastern origins to modern culture, covering its symbolism, art, psychology and media appearances.
key_facts: The gryphon has the body of a lion and the head and wings of an eagle and has fascinated people since ancient Egypt and Greece.
Historians trace the gryphon myth to the Near East, with figures appearing as early as the 3rd millennium BC, with Egyptian and Persian influences cited.
By the Middle Ages the gryphon was adopted into Christian iconography to represent Christ's dual nature, divine and human.
In medieval heraldry the gryphon symbolized strength, vigilance, and valor on coats of arms and banners.
Dante Alighieri depicted the gryphon in his "Divine Comedy" (1317), symbolizing the dual nature of Christ.
Lewis Carroll portrayed a gryphon as Alice's guide in "Alice's Adventures in Wonderland" (1865).
The 16th century text "Historiae Animalium" contains intricate engravings of the gryphon.
Perugia in Italy celebrates the gryphon as part of its heritage; its annual 'Festival of the Gryphon' on October 12, 2023 featured a parade with floats and performers in gryphon costumes.
Carl Jung and others examined the gryphon as an archetype of the psyche, with the lion representing earthly power and the eagle spiritual aspiration.
Jungian psychologist Helen Morrison said the gryphon archetype is about reconciling paradoxes within us, harmonizing base instincts with loftier aims.
The streaming series "Guardians of the Cipher" debuts in September 2024, featuring gryphons protecting an ancient code capable of altering reality; creator and executive producer is James Thornton.

Philip Robertson, professor of mythology at Devinshire University, said on March 15, 2024 at a symposium that societal upheaval brings a resurgence of longing for mythological guardians like the gryphon.
Universities and financial bodies use the gryphon in their emblems as a symbol of authority and protection of knowledge and wealth.
